what_it_is: An American woman on death row in Tennessee for a murder she committed in 1995, when she was 18.
why_now: Tennessee tried to execute her on Wednesday night and failed. She survived two doses of the lethal injection drug and was taken to hospital, and Governor Bill Lee has halted the state's one remaining execution this year. She would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years, which is why her page had been climbing all week before it exploded.

what_it_is: The running count of gold, silver and bronze medals won by each country at the 2026 Asian Games.
why_now: The Asian Games are running in Aichi and Nagoya, Japan, until 4 October. People check the medal table like a league table: every day, and more often as the finals pile up in the last week.

what_it_is: The page that tracks India's athletes and results at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan.
why_now: India sent 495 athletes and English Wikipedia has a huge Indian readership, so this page tracks the medal table closely. It got an extra push when Vithya Ramraj broke P. T. Usha's national record in the 400 m hurdles, a mark that had stood since the 1984 Olympics. Her own page entered the top 100 the same day.

what_it_is: The name given to seven Cornell University fraternity members accused in a 2024 sexual assault case.
why_now: A brand-new article. In mid-September a former Cornell student sued the university and seven members of its Chi Phi fraternity, alleging she was drugged and raped at the fraternity house in 2024. The nickname spread on social media, the local prosecutor reopened the criminal investigation, and Wikipedia now has a page for the case. These are allegations, and at least one of the men has denied them through his lawyer.

what_it_is: Asia's biggest multi-sport event, held every four years. This edition is in Aichi and Nagoya, Japan.
why_now: The main article for the same event. Three of the top five pages are the Asian Games, which tells you how much of English Wikipedia's audience is in Asia.

what_it_is: An American woman tried and acquitted of killing her father and stepmother with an axe in 1892.
why_now: Netflix's Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story. Viewers finish an episode and go check what really happened in Fall River in 1892. The page is sliding down from 806,000 ten days ago, the classic curve after a streaming premiere. The series page and lead actress Ella Beatty are both further down the top 100.

what_it_is: The American mathematician known as the Unabomber, who ran a years-long bombing campaign. He died in 2023.
why_now: Netflix released Unabomber, with Russell Crowe, on 25 September. His page appeared on the chart that day, peaked two days later and is easing off now.

what_it_is: An American actor and director, Emmy winner for Life Goes On, and the younger brother of Rob Lowe.
why_now: A sad one. The actor and his wife, producer Kim Painter, confirmed on Wednesday that their 13-year-old daughter Fiona has died. His brother Rob Lowe's page rose the same day.

what_it_is: A psychology concept: the ability to understand that other people have beliefs, desires and thoughts different from your own.
why_now: I couldn't find a news hook. When an academic psychology article jumps to 183,000 views in one day, it's usually a viral post linking to it, a quiz or puzzle answer, or automated traffic. Nothing in the coverage I checked points to which.

what_it_is: The photo and video sharing app owned by Meta.
why_now: Also unsolved. Big brand pages like this sometimes jump when an outage or an app change sends people searching, and sometimes it's bots. I found no clear trigger for Wednesday.

what_it_is: An English journalist and television presenter, a household name in Britain since the 1970s.
why_now: The British broadcaster died on 30 September, aged 86. She presented That's Life! on the BBC for 21 years and founded the children's helpline Childline. Her late husband Desmond Wilcox entered the top 100 too, as readers clicked through from her page.

what_it_is: An internet domain ending, like .com, created for adult websites.
why_now: No news here. This page about a web domain has sat between 115,000 and 205,000 views a day for well over a week. Real curiosity comes in spikes and then fades. A level line like this points to automated traffic or mistyped web addresses landing on Wikipedia.

what_it_is: Wikipedia's running list of notable people who have died this year.
why_now: It never leaves the list. Around 140,000 people check who has died, every single day, with almost no variation. It is the steadiest line on the page.

what_it_is: A 2026 satirical black comedy film directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu, starring Tom Cruise.
why_now: Views tripled in two days, the pattern you get when reviews land and a release is close. I didn't verify the exact release date, so take the timing as an educated read of the curve.

article: Dancing with the Stars (American TV series) season 35
what_it_is: The current season of the American TV contest that pairs celebrities with professional dancers.
why_now: Tuesday night is episode night on ABC, and the page spikes right after. Look at the chart: one bump a week ago, another now. People come to see who danced what and who went home.

what_it_is: An American serial killer who shot seven men in Florida in 1989 and 1990. She was executed in 2002.
why_now: A slow fade instead of a spike. My best guess is spillover: the Lizzie Borden series has people reading about other women accused of murder, and coverage of Christa Pike kept mentioning the few women executed in the US, Wuornos among them. I can't prove either link.

what_it_is: A first baseman for the New York Yankees baseball team.
why_now: Two home runs, one of them a grand slam, and six RBIs as the Yankees beat the Red Sox 9-0 in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series. Boston is his hometown team, which made the story even better.

what_it_is: The American prosecutor who, as special counsel, led the federal investigations into Donald Trump.
why_now: The former special counsel testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday. The hearing went viral because of one exchange with Senator Eric Schmitt, next on this list.

what_it_is: A Republican US senator from Missouri, in office since 2023.
why_now: The Missouri senator accused Jack Smith of lying about being at an Atlanta Hawks game. Smith had been at an Iowa Hawkeyes college game in Maryland. Schmitt had mixed up the two teams, and the clip spread fast. Senator Katie Britt's stunned face beside him became its own meme and put her page in the top 30.

what_it_is: A general-purpose internet domain ending, like .com.
why_now: Same story as .xxx: a page about a web domain ending with tens of thousands of daily views and no news behind it. Almost certainly automated traffic.

what_it_is: A tiny unincorporated community in Adair County, Kentucky.
why_now: A place this small does not get 80,000 real readers a day. The line has been flat for more than a week, so this is very likely a bot or a link baked into some app or device.

what_it_is: An English professional wrestler, real name Benjamin Satterley, known as Neville in WWE and Pac in AEW.
why_now: The English wrestler, known as Neville in WWE and Pac in AEW, died on 27 September at 40. His page hit 807,000 views when the news broke and is tailing off, the usual shape for an unexpected death.

what_it_is: A 2026 psychological thriller about the making of the reality TV show To Catch a Predator.
why_now: Robert Pattinson plays the show's host, Chris Hansen. Views peaked around 26 September and are fading, which fits a film in its first week out. Chris Hansen's own page is in the top 100 as well.

what_it_is: An Indian cricketer who captains the national team in Tests and one-day internationals.
why_now: He scored 223 not out off 133 balls as India chased down 406 against West Indies in Guwahati. It was only the second successful chase of 400 or more in one-day international history. The list of highest ODI scores started trending at the same time.

what_it_is: A 25-year-old starting pitcher for the New York Yankees.
why_now: The other half of the Yankees story. He threw 6.1 scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts against Boston, the team he grew up supporting.
